Date November 14, 1935.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. File No. D. 5589 Date 14-11-35）

Subject Letter from H.B.M. Consulate-General re communist suspect
TONG CHUN I (童春意).
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [签名]

With reference to the attached file on the above
subject, I have to report that efforts made by the Chinese
detectives attached to Section 2 have as yet failed to establish
the identity of the suspect Tong Chun I (童春意), which name,
it is believed, to be an alias of Giau Tek Hum (饒狄云),
a prominent member of the Malayan Communist Party.
Chok Siew Chok (鄒兆作) alias Tseu Zao Tsoh
(兆作), the communication agent mentioned in H.B.M.
Consulate letter of June 12, 1935, is still employed in the
Current Account Department of the Kok Hoa Bank (國華銀行),
better known as the China State Bank, No.356 Peking Road, and
continuous to reside with his wife and family at No.13, Lane
233, Markham Road. A general observation has been kept on
his movements but nothing of a suspicious nature discovered.
The local Government Censors who were requested
sometime ago to intercept mail addressed to Chow Siew Chok,
and to pass same over to the Municipal Police for examination,
have so far been unable to furnish any useful information.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE File No. 5389 S. B. D. 5389 6 8 35）
Date August 6, 1935.
Subject Letter from H.B.M. Consulate-General re communist suspect TONG CHUN I
( 童春志 )。
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by D.S.I. Byrne

With reference to the address -- "Tong Chun I, c/o Mr.
Choh Siew Chok ( 鄒兆作 ), Kok Hoa Bank ( 國華 ), Shanghai" --
which is reported to be in use by certain members of the Malayan
Communist Party, I have to report that enquiries made have so
far been without result.
Tong Chun I is believed to be an alias used by a well-
known member of the Malayan Communist Party named Giau Tek Hun
( 饒狄雲 ) in order to cloak his identity. Although this
communication address has been in the possession of the Municipal
Police since July 1934, no concrete evidence has yet been
obtained to warrant any action. The characters of the name
of the communication agent Chok Siew Chok are identical with
those in the Tseu Zao Tsoh ( 鄒兆作 ), who was often mentioned
in previous reports. The latter is still in the employ of
the Deposit Department of the Kok Hoa Bank ( 國華 ) which is
better known as the China State Bank, No.356 Peking Road, and
is staying with his wife and family in a downstairs room of
house No.13, Lane 233, Markham Road. Tseu was recently kept
under observation by Chinese detectives attached to this
Section, but his movements revealed nothing.
Another communication address of Tong Chun I, known to
the Municipal Police, is the Shanghai Bookstore, No.8, Lane 36,
North Honan Road, whose head office is in Singapore. This shop
occupies the ground portion of that address and employs five
assistants, all of whom are natives of Ningpo. None of these
resides in the French Concession or is known to be friendly
with persons residing in Avenue Dubail.
Following the receipt of the attached communication,
the local Government Censors were requested to intercept

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 5589
Date 17/8/34

Subject (in full) Letter dated July 16, 1934, from H.B.M. Consulate-General
re communist suspects Tong Chun I (童春意) et al.
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [Signature] A/.

Exhaustive enquiries made concerning two communist
suspects named Tseu Zao Tsok(鄒兆作) and Giau Tek Hun(饒狄云)
elicit the information that latter is believed to assume the
alias of Tong Chun I (童春意) in order to cloak his identity.
Tseu Zao Tsok, an employee in the Deposit Department
of the China State Bank, 356 Peking Road, who is suspected of
having received mail matter on behalf of Giau Tek Hun, member
of the Malayan Communist Party, is at present living with his
wife and family in the home of his friend named Nying Tsoh Jung
(任卓群), age about 32, native of Wusieh, employee of the
branch office of the "Bank of Kiangsu" in that city, at No.20
Si Tek Li "步德里"(Lane 233) Markham Road. They occupy the
ground portion of the premises. The reason for Tseu's removal
from his former address - No.4, Lane 233, Markham Road - is
attributable to a reduction of the monthly allowance granted
by his elder brother who is a prominent shareholder of the China
State Bank and who is also connected with several other local
Chinese banks.

A general watch kept on the movements of Tseu Zao Tsok,
his possible visitors as well as mail matter received by him has
so far failed to disclose anything of a suspicious nature. Very
few letters addressed to him have been observed and these
generally appear to be of a friendly nature and usually emanate
from his relatives in Kwangtung and Hongkong.

House No.4, Lane 233, Markham Road, which was formerly
occupied by Tseu has been rented by one named Mao(茅), an
employee of the Dah Chong(大昌) Dispensary, Foochow Road,
since August 1, 1934.

Further discreet enquiries made in the neighbourhood

P.O. BOX 289.    SHANGHAI.
No. D. 5589
Date 16 / 7 / 34

July 16th 1934.

My dear Robertson,

Many thanks for your letter No.D. 5589 of 13.7.34.
and its interesting enclosure.

I hope you will follow up this matter, it looks very
much as though both Tong Chun I and Giau Tek Hun may be names used by
Tseu Zao Tsoh and I shall be very interested to received any further
information you may obtain in this connection.

Yours sincerely.
H. Middleton

T. Robertson Esq.,
Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
Shanghai.

Dear Mr. Steptoe,

With reference to your letter of July 5,
1934, I forward herewith copy of a report regarding
one Tong Chun I (童春意) and two addresses in
Shanghai from which he sends letters to communists
in Singapore.

Yours sincerely,

Subject (in full) Letter dated July 5, 1934, from H.B.M.Consulate-General
regarding a communist suspect named Tong Chun I (童春意).
Made by D.I.Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [签名]

Discreet enquiries made by C.D.C.281 regarding a certain
Chinese communist suspect named Tong Chun I (童春意) who is using
the following accomodation addresses (1) No.4, Bek Si Tek Li,
Shanghai (上海麦根路世德里四号 ) and (2) c/o Shanghai Book Store,
Hong Fook Li, Tien Hau Kong Bridge, North Honan Road, Shanghai
(上海北河南路天后宫桥洪福里上海书局中庄转 ), elicit the following :
Address (1) is situate at No.S-4, Lane 233, Markham
Road and is occupied by Tseu Zao Tsoh (邹肇作), an employee of
the China State Bank, 356 Peking Road. There are no other
families residing at this address. It will be recalled that
in a previous enquiry from H.B.M. Consulate-General, Tseu is
suspected of having received mail matter on behalf of a well-
known member of the Malayan Communist Party named Giau Tek Hun
(饶狄云) (vide file D-5589).
Address (2) is located at No.8, Lane 36, North Honan
Road. It is the local agency of the Shanghai Bookstore in
Singapore and was established in 1932. There are five people
employed in this establishment. Confidential enquiries disclose
that the name Tong Chun I is unknown at this address.
It is therefore surmised that the name Tong Chun I
is an assumed name used by Giau Tek Hun particulars of whom
have already been reported.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch

P.C. BOX 250.    SHANGHAI
Date 11 / 7 / 34

5th July 1934.

My dear Robertson,

Letters have been intercepted at Singapore from a
certain Tong Chun I (童春意) who is using the following accomodation
addresses in Shanghai.

1.  No. 4, Bek Si Tek Li.,
    Shanghai.
    上海麥根路世德里四號

2.  c/o Shanghai Book Store,    上海書局中庄轉
    Hong Fook Li,               洪福里
    Tien Hau Kong Bridge,       天后宮橋
    North Honan Road,           北河南路
    Shanghai.                   上海

This man is suspected of being a member of the
Students' Federation in Malaya, is an ex-student of the Singapore
Chinese High School, and corresponds with known communists.  Amongst
others he corresponds with a woman named Tiun Kui Liong, who is head
of the Women's Federation and also a known communist.

I shall be glad if you will let me know any information you may
be able to obtain about this man and his activities in Shanghai.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]

T. Robertson Esq.,
Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police,

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S.B. REGISTRY. File No. D 5589 Date 5/7/34 3U）

Subject (in full) Letter dated 26.6.34 from H.B.M. Consulate-General re:
Giau Tek Hun (饒秋雲) and Tseu Zao Tsoh (肇作).
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by （签名） D.I.

Discreet enquiries made by C.D.S. 48 regarding Giau Tek
Hun (饒秋雲), a member of the Malayan Communist Party, who is
reported to have been residing at Tien Po Li (天寶里), No.35,
Lane 789, North Chengtu Road elicit the following :-
The address "Tien Po Li, No.35, Lane 789 North Chengtu
Road, Shanghai" is a double-house situate in Lane 879 North
Chengtu Road and not Lane 789. The tenant of the premises
is one Sung Ching-foh (孫正福), a carriage hong proprietor,
who formerly resided at 791 Myburgh Road until November 1933
and who occupies the upstairs front room in the right wing.
The upstair back wing room is sub-let to Pan Zien-sung (潘全生),
a chauffeur in the employ of a local Japanese. Pan is at
present attending to some domestic affairs in his native
place at Chenju. The upstair portion as well as the downstairs
front room of the premises are rented by the Ching Foh Daung
(正福堂) Joss House, while the room above the kitchen has
been occupied since November last by Tsang Tsing-sz (張清思),
age 42, a native of Soochow, employed as a clerk with the
Gold Bar Exchange, No.69 Kiukiang Road. Another sub-tenant
named Zung Tung-sung (陳東生), architect, age 38, native of
Nanziang, is living in the downstairs front room, while the back-
room is tenanted by C.D.C. 231 Ung Fah Ling (杭法林) attached
to Chengtu Road Station.
Giau Tek Hun is not known to the occupants of the
house nor has anyone answering to his description been seen
visiting the premises.
Although the exact relations between Giau Tek Hun and
Tseu Zao Tsoh, an employee of the China State Bank, 356 Peking
Road, and occupant of house No.S-4, Lane 233, Markham Road,

June 26th 1934.

My dear Robertson,

On 27.12.33 I addressed to Mr. Givens a letter
on the subject of one Gian Tek Han, to-gether with a copy of the
mans photograph. This man is a member of the Malayan Communist
party and I now have reason to believe that he is residing at
Tien Po Li, No.35, Lane 789 North Chengtu Road, Shanghai.

Would you have this address investigated please
and endeavour to discover this man's relations with 非作
of the China State Bank, Peking Road, No. 2S - 4, Lane 233 Markham
Road.

Yours sincerely,
Huléphé

Made by....................and................................Forwarded by......D. I.......Everest

With reference to report dated January 16, 1934, regarding
a member of the Singapore Communist Party named Giau Tek Hun
(饒狄雲), further efforts to locate this person in Shanghai
have been unsuccessful.
Tseu Zao Tsoh(鄒兆作), employee of the China State Bank,
Peking Road, who is stated to receive letters addressed to Giau
Tek Hun has been kept under observation for the past two weeks
but without result.
Particulars of Giau Tek Hun and Tseu Zao Tsoh have been
recorded for future reference.

REPORT
File No............
Date January 16, 19 34.

Subject (in full) Letter from H.B.M. Consulate-General dated 27/12/33 regarding
NGAU DIH YUEN TSEU ZAO TSOH
Giau Tek Hun (饒狄雲), c/o Chiau Tiau Chok (趙兆作).

Made by and Forwarded by D.I. Everest.

With reference to the attached letter from H.B.M. Consulate-
General dated December 27, 1933, regarding the presence in Shanghai
of a member of the Singapore Communist Party named Giau Tek Han
(饒狄雲) (Shanghai romanization Ngau Dih Yuen) who is stated
to be using the following communication address: c/o Tseu Zao Tsoh
(新兆作), China State Bank, Shanghai, I have to state that
despite diligent enquiries by the staff of this office Giau Tek
Han has not yet been located.

It has been ascertained, however, that Tseu Zao Tsoh, who is
an employee of the China State Bank, Peking Road, resides at
No.s-4, Lane 233, Markham Road. A watch has been kept on his
movements but nothing of interest has so far been observed.

Tseu Zao Tsoh first came to the notice of this office in
October, 1933, when it was discovered that he acted as guarantor
to two suspected communists employed in the now defunct South
China News Agency named Wong Tsai Kwang (王才光) and Zao Feh
Kwang (邹拂塵), who then resided in a room at No.229 Markham Road.
This address was raided by the Municipal Police at the request of
the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety on October 12, 1933. Nothing
of an incriminating nature was found in the room and the two
suspects were released after being questioned.

Enquiries are proceeding.

D. I.

S.●
HR
Officer i/c Special Branch.

BRITISH CONSULATE-GENERAL,
P.O.B. 255. SHANGHAI

27th December 1933

My dear Givens,

I enclose herewith copy of a letter
intercepted in Singapore, written by a man named
GIAU TEK HAN, who was a member of the Communist
Party in Singapore. He bolted to Shanghai when
his house was raided in September this year. I
enclose herewith this man's photograph. You will
notice that in this letter reference is made to the
newspaper business and that this has been stopped.
I think this must refer to the recent raid by the
French Police in connection with the South China
News Agency.

Yours sincerely,
（签名）

T.P.Givens, Esq.,
Special Branch,
S.M.P.

S2, For attention please
JMS

（照片）

Copy of Intercepted letter
Friends, Ban, He, Su and Hiap (漫, 霞, 樹, 俠)
Since I left Singapore I have now come to Shanghai, I have already sent you a letter and I think you must have received it. I am sorry that I have to leave in such a hurry and was unable to inform any of you but I think all of you will excuse me.
The coming New Year Holidays remind me of your activities of next year. But why should we be worried or frightened if we can help each other as we have done in the past. At present the only thing which I wish to know is your activities of next year, so please let me know in your reply.
Has He's family returned home ? How about Su's lover ? I have received two letters from Ban of the 9th and 12the Sept. and from which I know that all of you remember of me very much. That sum of money which you have sent me is indeed a great help to me. I know that the money has been sent to Mr Bun Thai (敏泰) as he had already informed me and he is going to remit it to me very soon.
How is the health of He, is he alright now ? Has Ban gone to Singapore and on what occasion does he go? It is a pity that I could not see him but circumstances have made it so. What can we do.
Our newspaper businesses have already started but unfortunately we were forced to stop it for some time. We are now going to carry on with the business again. We have decided to publish daily papers and after everything is settled we will publish other periodicals.
My address is (Yen Zao Yoh)
Giau Tek Hun (饒狄雲)
C/o Chiau Tiau Ghok (非作)
C/o Kok Hoa Bank,
Shanghai.
Ngan Dih Yun Yours,
Tek (狄 )
25.11.33
